phrases.english_text: They were living better. Because there was water inside the house. But they used firewood. I think just about everybody used firewood. We were cutting wood, my nephew and I. And we were selling them for heating, four dollars for half a rick. But five dollars a rick to cook with. We felt good about it, back then. There was nothing else to do. I mentioned I was working at Greenleaf. They gave us Piecework… May Sanders, Melvin Campbell—we were setting the flower pots. And the more rows we finished we got a one-hundred and twenty [dollar] check. We really felt good about it, back then. It was really good getting paid like that. But today, it’s not as good. You can’t buy anything with just that much money. We were in a bad spot because we couldn’t afford college. That’s what is lacking. These young kids need to go to college, they are using too many drugs nowadays. If they go to college—I’m not saying it will stop—but they could get something from it. There are a lot of things nowadays. But as we were growing up… The children are not doing exercise today. They are just watching their phones. They are sitting like this [indicates] they probably don’t even know we came to visit or not. Cause they are just watching the phone. I’m not saying I’m different because sometimes I watch my phone too. I mean, when it’s something important, but not just to play with it. Back then, we always found something to do. There was an owl that flew by, we chased it and my neighbor had a big dog. That’s the one that chased the owl, and when it landed on a tree the dog would tree it and we would throw rocks at it. One day, it fell from the tree when it got wore out, that owl. That’s all we had to do, but we were having fun.

phrases.english_text: One time me and my nephew were walking to the store. It was about a mile from the house. Somebody gave us a ride. phrases.english_text: Most of all, the grass was tall all the time. And that’s where we crawled around playing hide-and-seek. They used to play kick-the-can. And when night came, and when somebody kicked their can close to the fire, they would count them. And when another kicked their’s to the fire, they were way over there, then we turned it loose. And we had to get out [of the game]. That’s what we were doing growing up. Paul Cooksey and his mom. That’s where we lived and we grew up with them. There were a lot of things to do. But they were the only ones that had a TV. And we went over there when we wanted to watch something. For me, it was okay for them to have a TV. I didn’t get mad about it.

And we had to get out [of the game]. That’s what we were doing growing up. Paul Cooksey and his mom. That’s where we lived and we grew up with them. There were a lot of things to do. phrases.english_text: We believed in Santa Claus for a long time. One time I realized. We were in bed near our parents, but somehow the others got a better present than me. phrases.phonetic_broad: nustetiwtyo vna aseskin
phrases.english_text: It’s still going to be there. But nobody wants to work. There are only Hispanics working there now. There aren’t going to be any job opportunities because they’re opening the border for too many different people, that are coming in. That’s what Lawrence used to say, also, “That’s what the Bible says, ‘there will be a lot of different nationalities coming in, and they are going to eat up the food,’ Lawrence used to say when he preached. I guess it is written somewhere. Everything is going to run out. That’s why you need to go to college. But also there are no jobs for them, even when they finish college. They just hunt around but can’t find anything. But most of all, maybe you should learn a trade. Like at a votech. Like refrigerator or A/C repairmen training—they do find good jobs. Also, they have their own company. I know one Indian man. That’s what he does. Sometimes he gets sent and it’s unusual for a native to have a job like that. I don’t know…
